_comment: The partitioned 30 Hz chain as an engineer with an accelerator and no per-shape profiling would deploy it: BLANKET IME. yolo is pinned to CPU_P#0-3 (machine_width 4) as in wh_chain30_part4ime, and prefer_impls holds every one of its dispatches that HAS an IME kernel on the matrix engine (the 35 add/cat/maxpool/upsample dispatches have none and keep RVV, exactly as the forced binary does) rather than letting the solver take the cheaper cell per dispatch -- a per-dispatch cost model cannot express this deployment, because a solver handed both options always picks the winner. gen_root is gen_mb_force, whose yolo ime_x60 cells are the MB_IME_FORCE=1 build's own measured per-dispatch costs against the same RVV baseline (63 of 90 rows, 46 of them faster than RVV and 17 slower at four harts -- the forced build runs them on the engine either way); nav and control keep gen_mb_shard's cells and stay on RVV. The board run must set MB_IME_FORCE=1 so the binary matches these costs.

chain.deadline_rationale: a frame's goal reaches control within its nav window (77.8 ms); control is phase-locked at 100 Hz and acts on the newest goal
